summary: Teams of 2-4 students create and submit a comprehensive business plan for a new enterprise in their local area, including supporting documents. After qualifying, teams present their plan virtually to judges and answer questions. The event focuses on business development, organizational structure, and strategic planning.
time_limits: Setup: no more than three (3) minutes
Presentation: no more than ten (10) minutes
Judges’ questions: no more than five (5) minutes
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing Business Plan, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Submission must be uploaded to https://upload.bpa.org
deadlines: Event registration deadline: no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
Submission deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Demonstrate understanding of enterprise development and organizational scaling
Communicate and present research persuasively, both orally and in writing
Identify and leverage internal/external resources for growth
Develop a comprehensive, scalable business plan (operations and long-term strategy)
Analyze target markets and develop a customer acquisition/retention strategy
Apply strategic pricing and analyze financials (revenue, capital, ROI)
Design an organizational structure for delegation, leadership, and efficiency

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.
Business Plan did not exceed ten (10) pages single-sided. The Title Page, Table of Contents, and Works Cited are not included in the ten (10) page limit.
Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing Business Plan, Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual), BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.
Management and Ownership of the Business
rubric.description: Comprehensive organizational chart with detailed roles.
In-depth analysis, strong edge, justified pricing.
Plan is exceptionally well-organized, concise, and complete.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, with a mostly clear structure and smooth transitions between points.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.

Teams who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Teams participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
Only the team captain should complete the submission.
